overview: Two opposing metabolic pathways that break down or build up glucose, tightly regulated so they don't run simultaneously in the same cell.
genZNote: Glycolysis tears glucose apart. Gluconeogenesis builds it back from scraps.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: The breakdown of one glucose molecule into two pyruvate molecules, generating ATP and NADH.
aspects.valueB: The synthesis of new glucose from non-carbohydrate precursors such as lactate, glycerol, or amino acids.

aspects.label: Net Energy Change
aspects.valueA: Net gain of 2 ATP and 2 NADH per glucose.
aspects.valueB: Net cost of 6 ATP equivalents per glucose synthesized.

aspects.label: Primary Location
aspects.valueB: Mainly liver (and kidney cortex during prolonged fasting).

aspects.label: Key Regulatory Enzymes
aspects.valueB: Pyruvate carboxylase, PEP carboxykinase, fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase, glucose-6-phosphatase.

aspects.label: Reciprocal Regulation
aspects.valueA: Activated by insulin/fed state; inhibited by high ATP/citrate.
aspects.valueB: Activated by glucagon/cortisol/fasting state; inhibited by insulin, ensuring the two pathways are not both fully active at once.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueB: Builds glucose up from non-carbohydrate sources.
